title: 2007 AMC 10A Problem 10
statement: The Dunbar family consists of a mother, a father, and some children. The average age of the members of the family is \(20,\) the father is \(48\) years old, and the average age of the mother and children is \(16.\) How many children are in the family?

solutions.text:
Let \(N\) be the number of children and \(T\) the total age of the family.

Then \(20 = \dfrac{T}{N + 2}\) and \(16 = \dfrac{T - 48}{N + 1}.\)

These give \(20N + 40 = T\) and \(16N + 64 = T,\) so \(20N + 40 = 16N + 64.\)

Hence \(4N = 24\) and \(N = 6.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let \(N\) be the number of children; the family has \(N + 2\) members
The total age is \(20(N + 2);\) removing the father leaves \(16(N + 1)\)
